issues.failure_explanation: On each closed sub-interval $I^j$ the constructed $\phi$ rises by $h-\delta^\mu$ (the prefactor of $P$ in \eqref{shapfunc0}). Lemma \ref{Shape-Lemma0} asserts strict monotonicity with no hypothesis on $h$ versus $\delta^\mu$: for $h<\delta^\mu$ the prefactor $(h-\delta^\mu)/(h-\delta)$ is negative and $\phi$ decreases on every $I^j$; for $h=\delta^\mu$ it is constant on every $I^j$, so $\phi$ is not strictly increasing. The proof step invoking $S'(z),P'(z)>0$ ignores this prefactor. Theorem \ref{Inner-Lemma} assumes only $h\ge\delta^\mu$, so at equality (the value used in the numerical sections, $\mu=1/2$, $\delta=1/N^2$) $\psi_q$ is constant on all sub-intervals: it is not strictly increasing and $\psi_q'\equiv0$ on the $I_q^j$, contradicting the claim that $\psi_q'$ vanishes only at endpoints and the advertised property that the derivatives do not vanish on the disjoint closed sub-intervals.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the strict hypothesis $h>\delta^\mu$ to Lemma \ref{Shape-Lemma0} and Theorem \ref{Inner-Lemma} (noting that the numerical choice $h=\delta^\mu$ then sits at the excluded boundary); all bounds, constructions and rates are unaffected.
issues.overall_effect: The headline strict monotonicity and non-flatness of the inner functions (abstract, introduction item (i)) fail in the degenerate case allowed by the hypotheses and actually used in the numerics, where the construction degenerates to the staircase pathology the paper criticizes in Igelnik-Parikh.
issues.title: Strict monotonicity and non-vanishing derivative of the inner functions fail when h <= delta^mu

issues.failure_explanation: $\phi$ satisfies $\phi(t+h)=\phi(t)+h$, hence $\phi(1+s)-\phi(s)=1$ holds only if $1$ is an integer multiple of $h$, i.e. $Jh=1$. Theorem \ref{MainResult} assumes only $J=\lceil 1/h\rceil$, which permits $Jh>1$; e.g. $h=0.3$, $\delta=0.15$, $\mu=1$, $q=2$ gives $\phi(0.85)-\phi(-0.15)\approx1.0185\neq1$. The asserted identity, and with it the second equality in \eqref{PsiqxAS} (normalizing denominator $=1$), is therefore false in general. The normalized $\psi_q$ then differs by a non-unit factor from the unnormalized difference $\phi(x+(1-q)\delta)-\phi((1-q)\delta)$ used in all subsequent explicit formulas (Lemma \ref{lmm:aqj-formula}, including the step \eqref{ajJ-21} which tacitly needs $Jh=1$, and Lemma \ref{SprecherLambda}) and in the range claim of Theorem \ref{Inner-Lemma}; the closing equality $h^\alpha=1/J^\alpha$ in \eqref{approximA} also needs $Jh=1$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume $1/h\in\mathbb{N}$ (as Algorithm \ref{Constructive_alg} already does), or carry the normalizing factor $\phi(1+(1-q)\delta)-\phi((1-q)\delta)$ through all formulas; every statement then survives with constant-factor changes.
issues.overall_effect: The definition of the inner functions and the explicit formulas for the images $a_q^{\bs j}$, the row-spacing estimates and the non-interlacing lemma are reliable only under $Jh=1$, which the main theorem's $J=\lceil 1/h\rceil$ does not guarantee (the algorithm, in contrast, assumes it).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we can show that all $a_q^{\bs j}$ are distinct if $\lambda_p$ are rationally independent, which can be verified readily by examining the difference $a_q^{\bs j}-a_{q'}^{{\bs j}'}$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's premise that the sampled values $y_{j_p}=\psi_q(c_q^{j_p})$ are 'all rational numbers' is false in general: $y_{j_p}=j_ph+C_q$ with $C_q=\frac{3h-\delta^\mu}{2}-(h-\delta^\mu)P(\frac{N-q}{N-1})$ (by \eqref{phi-delta}), which involves $\delta^\mu$ and is irrational for generic parameters. A collision $a_q^{\bs j}=a_q^{\bs j'}$ is a relation $\sum_p\lambda_pw_p=0$ with coefficients $w_p$ built from $h$, $1$ and $C_q$; rational independence excludes only relations with rational coefficients. When $C_q/h\notin\mathbb{Q}$ one can choose positive, normalized, rationally independent $\lambda$ on the resulting hyperplane: for $d=2$, $J\ge3$, take (normalized) $\lambda_1=C_q$, $\lambda_2=h+C_q$; then $\lambda_1/\lambda_2\notin\mathbb{Q}$ yet $a_q^{(1,-1)}=\lambda_1(h+C_q)=\lambda_2C_q=a_q^{(-1,0)}$. So the proposition is false as stated, and the 'readily verified' claim of Remark \ref{dist-again} inherits the same gap (the differences have irrational coefficients).

issues.failure_explanation: The bounds \eqref{Nsquare2} and \eqref{NonCsquare} require $(\Psi_q(\bs x)-\tau_k)/(\tau_{k+1}-\tau_k)\in[0,1]$, i.e. $\Psi_q(\bs x)\in T_k$ where $\tau_k=a_q^{\bs j}$ is the image of the centre of the hypercube containing (or closest to) $\bs x$ and $\tau_{k+1}$ its selected neighbour; then $|S(\cdot)|\le1$ is used. This containment is never proved and is false under the theorem's hypotheses: $\Psi_q$ oscillates by up to $|\bs\lambda|_1(h-\delta^\mu)$ over a single hypercube (each $\psi_q$ rises $h-\delta^\mu$ on every $I_q^j$; Lemma \ref{disjointlem} states exactly this), while the nearest-neighbour spacing is only $\lambda_p\min\{h,(h+\delta^\mu)/2\}$. For the Sprecher-like weights of Remark \ref{Cond-lambda} ($\lambda_p=O(N^{p-d})$), e.g. $d=2$, $J=N$, $\delta=N^{-2}$, $\mu\in(1/2,1)$, $\lambda_1\approx1/(2N)$, $\lambda_2\approx1$, a vertex point of a cube has $|\Psi_q(\bs x)-a_q^{\bs j}|\approx(h-\delta^\mu)/2$, exceeding $|T_k|=\lambda_1h$ by a factor $\sim N$. The $S$-argument then lies outside $[0,1]$, where neither $S$ (defined on $[0,1]$) nor the piecewise formula \eqref{qj2g} (defined only on $T_k$) applies: $(g_q\circ\Psi_q)(\bs x)$, Algorithm step III(ii) and the bound $|S(\cdot)|\le1$ are all unjustified; Remark \ref{remk-Slides} merely asserts the needed avoidance without proof. Under the natural repair (interpolating on the interval that actually contains $\Psi_q(\bs x)$), the bracketing nodes correspond to centres at distance $\Theta(1)$ from $\bs x$, giving per-level error $\Theta(1/N)$ and total $\Theta(1)$ rather than $O(h^\alpha)$; the analysis is valid only in the near-degenerate regime $\delta^\mu\approx h$ where $\psi_q$ is essentially constant on the sub-intervals.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum a repair must define $g_q(\Psi_q(\bs x))$ for every $\bs x$ via intervals that provably contain $\Psi_q(\bs x)$ (e.g. neighbours in a large-$\lambda$ direction with the side chosen by the sign of $\Psi_q(\bs x)-a_q^{\bs j}$), add a coupling constraint such as $|\bs\lambda|_1(h-\delta^\mu)\le\lambda_d(h+\delta^\mu)/2$ (forcing $\delta^\mu\gtrsim h^2$, i.e. $\mu$ confined to a narrow window near the degenerate value), treat gap levels separately, and re-prove the per-level bounds. Every such route either restricts to the near-degenerate regime, where the inner functions are nearly flat on the sub-intervals, or gives up the single-valued $C^2$ outer function.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central deliverable is unestablished: $f_N$ is not well defined by the stated selection rule; the error bounds \eqref{Nsquare2}-\eqref{NonCsquare}, hence \eqref{approximA} and the advertised accuracy $O(N^{-\alpha(1+\gamma)})$ (abstract, introduction item (iii)), are unproved; Algorithm \ref{Constructive_alg} step III(ii) cannot be executed as specified; the $C^2$ character of the superposition is unsupported for the per-point selection. The trailing Theorems \ref{Contructconvergence} and \ref{KSNconvergence} build on the same construction and are reported separately for their own additional defects.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims an open problem that does not exist. The paper's shape functions are chosen so that the first two derivatives vanish at the endpoints; replacing the exponent $2$ in \eqref{P-fun} by $3$ (the normalized integral $\int_0^z\tau^3(1-\tau)^3d\tau$, a degree-7 smoothstep) gives a function with all properties \eqref{Pproperty} plus vanishing third derivatives, and $S_3(z)=z-\frac{2}{3\pi}\sin(2\pi z)+\frac{1}{12\pi}\sin(4\pi z)$ satisfies $S_3'=\frac23(\cos(2\pi z)-1)^2\ge0$ with $S_3(0)=0$, $S_3(1)=1$, $S_3(1/2)=1/2$ and derivatives up to order three vanishing at both ends. Hence $C^3$ (indeed $C^k$ for any $k$) shape functions exist by a trivial modification of the paper's own pattern, so the claimed uncertainty is false.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement asserts a representation with locally $C^2$ outer functions, but the key step \eqref{Nsquare} asserts the equality $g_q(\Psi_q(\bs x))=b_q^{\bs j}$, which holds only for the piecewise-constant outer function of \eqref{gqaverage}, a discontinuous object that is not $C^2$. For the actual $S$-interpolated outer functions an interpolation-error term is required and is nowhere estimated. In addition, the factor $(1+2^\alpha/d^{\alpha/2})$ in the final display appears without derivation, the $q\notin Q$ term relies on \eqref{N3f}, which is derived later under extra assumptions ($\mu\ge1/2$ and $\tau_{\min}$ bounds that tacitly use $|\bs\lambda|_1=1$), and \eqref{Oscf} bounds the distance to the nearest centre by $\sqrt dN\delta/2$ where it can be $\sqrt d(N+1)\delta/2$. Thus the $O(1/N)$ bound is established only for a construction the statement does not allow; this mismatch is independent of, and survives repair of, the underlying interval-containment defect of the construction.

issues.failure_explanation: If $g_q^s$ and $\psi_q^s$ are quadratic, each summand $g_q^s(\sum_i\lambda_i\psi_q^s(x_i))$ is a polynomial of degree at most $4$ in $\bs x$, hence so is $f_N^s$: the approximants lie in a fixed finite-dimensional space independent of $N$ and cannot approximate an arbitrary $f\in C(I^d)$ with error $O(1/N)$ (for e.g. $f(x)=\sin(\pi x_1)$ the error does not even tend to $0$). The supporting estimates assert $\|g_q-g_q^s\|=O(M^{-4})=O(N^{-2})$ (with $M=O(\sqrt N)$ nodes) and $\|\psi_q-\psi_q^s\|=O(N^{-2})$ with no argument: impossible for quadratic approximants unless the targets are themselves quadratic, and unjustified for the constructed $g_q,\psi_q$, which are only globally $C^2$ (third derivatives jump at the glue points), so a fourth-order rate cannot hold. The final chain \eqref{estfminusfNs} also uses an undefined constant $L$ and the undefined reference '(3)'.
